克塞迪耶夫常以獨奏形式出現，也用於柬埔寨傳統婚禮樂團「普倫卡博蘭」、阿雷克樂團，: The kse diev often appears as a solo instrument, and is also used in the Cambodian traditional wedding ensemble, the phleng kar boran, in the arak ensemble, and in the healing ritual ensemble called phleng arak. These are mostly live performances, and the source lists no specific composers or pieces, so listening examples should be taken from these traditional line-ups and ritual music.
克塞迪耶夫為柬埔寨棒狀齊特琴，發聲體為一根銅或黃銅弦；共鳴器為葫蘆，以尼龍繩固定: The kse diev is a Cambodian stick zither; the sounding body is a single copper or brass string, and the resonator is a gourd tied to the stick with nylon cord, open at the other end. The nylon cord also forms the string loop that holds the string close to the stick. It is played with a tubular plectrum of copper or plastic. Another type, the kse muoy, adds a gourd at the bottom. The source does not state the wood, the dimensions or the materials of the other parts of the body.
克塞迪耶夫（Kse diev，又稱 khse mhoy）是柬埔寨弦鳴樂器，屬棒式: The kse diev (also called khse mhoy) is a Cambodian chordophone of the stick-zither type, with a single copper or brass string stretched on a wooden stick, a gourd resonator tied on with nylon cord, and the open end held against the chest. The player plucks the string with a tubular plectrum on the fourth finger and stops it with the first finger to change pitch, while the left hand opens and closes the resonator to shape the overtones. The tuning is usually A2 or G2, with a range of about twelve notes. It is used mostly for solo playing and also appears in the arak ensemble, the traditional wedding ensemble and the magic healing ensemble.
其音色來自單根銅或黃銅弦與葫蘆共鳴器；定弦為低音，常見十二音音域。演奏者以第四指: Its sound comes from a single copper or brass string and a gourd resonator; it is tuned low, with a range of twelve notes in the usual case. The player plucks the string with a tubular plectrum on the fourth finger, and the first finger presses and releases the string near the resonator to control the start of the note, the bends and the tail; opening and closing the resonator against the chest adjusts the overtones. The related kse muoy has one more gourd at the bottom, so the number of resonators differs.

演奏時將葫蘆共鳴器開口端貼住胸口，以套在第四指的銅或塑膠管狀撥片撥銅弦。第一指在: To play, hold the open end of the gourd resonator against the chest and pluck the copper string with the copper or plastic tubular plectrum worn on the fourth finger. The first finger stops the string near the gourd, moving up and down and pressing and releasing to start the note, bend it or control the tail. Opening and closing the left hand on the resonator against the chest adjusts the overtones. A beginner first practises the order: hold it against the chest, pluck, press, open and close.
聯合國協助柬埔寨評估文化資產時，克塞迪耶夫被視為最古老樂器。其最早圖像見於七世紀: When the United Nations helped Cambodia survey its cultural property, the kse diev was regarded as the oldest instrument. Its earliest image appears at Sambor Prei Kuk in the seventh century, later in reliefs at Bayon in the twelfth or thirteenth century, and it was played at the court of the Angkor empire. In the Khmer Rouge period of the 1970s very few players survived and the instrument almost disappeared. Sok Duch has taught pupils since 1979, so that new players have increased; competition from modern music still puts the traditional repertory under pressure.
